      "text": "To solve the differential equation $y\u0027 \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2} y}{x + \\sqrt{2} y}$, we can treat it as a **homogeneous first-order equation** or, more elegantly, as a **linear equation in $x$**.\n\n### Method: Solving for $x$ as a function of $y$\n\nThe given equation is:\n$$\\frac{dy}{dx} \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2} y}{x + \\sqrt{2} y}$$\n\nBy taking the reciprocal of both sides, we get the expression for $\\frac{dx}{dy}$:\n$$\\frac{dx}{dy} \u003d \\frac{x + \\sqrt{2} y}{\\sqrt{2} y}$$\n$$\\frac{dx}{dy} \u003d \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2} y} x + 1$$\n\nThis is a **linear first-order differential equation** for $x$ as a function of $y$, of the form $\\frac{dx}{dy} + P(y)x \u003d Q(y)$:\n$$\\frac{dx}{dy} - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2} y} x \u003d 1$$\n\n#### 1. Find the Integrating Factor\nThe integrating factor $\\mu(y)$ is:\n$$\\mu(y) \u003d e^{\\int -\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2} y} dy} \u003d e^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}} \\ln|y|} \u003d |y|^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n\n#### 2. Solve the Linear Equation\nMultiplying the entire equation by $\\mu(y)$:\n$$y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\frac{dx}{dy} - y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2} y} x \u003d y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n$$\\frac{d}{dy} \\left( x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\right) \u003d y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n\nNow, integrate both sides with respect to $y$:\n$$x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \u003d \\int y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} dy + C$$\nTo integrate $y^{-1/\\sqrt{2}}$, use the power rule $\\int y^n dy \u003d \\frac{y^{n+1}}{n+1}$:\n$$x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \u003d \\frac{y^{1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}}{1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C$$\n\n#### 3. Simplify the Result\nSimplify the denominator:\n$$1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}} \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2} - 1}{\\sqrt{2}}$$\nSo:\n$$x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2} - 1} y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C$$\n\nMultiply through by $y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$ to solve for $x$:\n$$x \u003d \\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2} - 1} \\right) y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\cdot y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n$$x \u003d \\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2} - 1} \\right) y^1 + C y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n\nFinally, rationalize the coefficient $\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2}-1}$:\n$$\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2}-1} \\cdot \\frac{\\sqrt{2}+1}{\\sqrt{2}+1} \u003d \\frac{2 + \\sqrt{2}}{2 - 1} \u003d 2 + \\sqrt{2}$$\n\n### General Solution\nThe general solution to the differential equation is:\n$$x \u003d (2 + \\sqrt{2})y + C y^{1/\\sqrt{2}}$$\n\nAlternatively, this can be written as:\n$$x - (2 + \\sqrt{2})y \u003d C y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{2}}$$ (depending on how you handle the exponent form). \n\n**Note:** $y \u003d 0$ and $y \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}x$ are also constant-ratio solutions that satisfy the original equation.",

        "text": "}}}$$\n$$\\frac{d}{dy} \\left( x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\"
      }, {
        "text": "right) \u003d y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n\nNow, integrate both sides with respect to $"
      }, {
        "text": "y$:\n$$x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \u003d \\int y^{-\\frac{1}{\\"
      }, {
        "text": "sqrt{2}}} dy + C$$\nTo integrate $y^{-1/\\sqrt{2}}$, use the power rule"
      }, {
        "text": " $\\int y^n dy \u003d \\frac{y^{n+1}}{n+1}$:\n$$x \\cdot y"
      }, {
        "text": "^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \u003d \\frac{y^{1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{"
      }, {
        "text": "2}}}}{1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C$$\n\n#### 3. Simplify the Result\nSimplify"
      }, {
        "text": " the denominator:\n$$1 - \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}} \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2}"
      }, {
        "text": " - 1}{\\sqrt{2}}$$\nSo:\n$$x \\cdot y^{-\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{"
      }, {
        "text": "2}}} \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2} - 1} y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{"
      }, {
        "text": "2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C$$\n\nMultiply through by $y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$"
      }, {
        "text": " to solve for $x$:\n$$x \u003d \\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2}"
      }, {
        "text": " - 1} \\right) y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}} \\cdot y^{\\"
      }, {
        "text": "frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}} + C y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n$$x"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d \\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2} - 1} \\right) y^"
      }, {
        "text": "1 + C y^{\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}}$$\n\nFinally, rationalize the coefficient $\\frac{\\sqrt"
      }, {
        "text": "{2}}{\\sqrt{2}-1}$:\n$$\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{\\sqrt{2}-1} \\cdot \\frac"
      }, {
        "text": "{\\sqrt{2}+1}{\\sqrt{2}+1} \u003d \\frac{2 + \\sqrt{2}}{"
      }, {
        "text": "2 - 1} \u003d 2 + \\sqrt{2}$$\n\n### General Solution\nThe general solution to the differential equation is"
      }, {
        "text": ":\n$$x \u003d (2 + \\sqrt{2})y + C y^{1/\\sqrt{2}}$$"
      }, {
        "text": "\n\nAlternatively, this can be written as:\n$$x - (2 + \\sqrt{2})y \u003d C"
      }, {
        "text": " y^{\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{2}}$$ (depending on how you handle the exponent form). \n\n**Note:**"
      }, {
        "text": " $y \u003d 0$ and $y \u003d \\frac{\\sqrt{2}-1}{\\sqrt{2}}x$ are also"
      }, {
        "text": " constant-ratio solutions that satisfy the original equation."
